summary: CCC-built 1934-35 steel tower and quarters in Mariposa County; abandoned by 2012, restoration status disputed, listed as standing.

facts.design: 41 ft steel tower with 7 ft x 7 ft metal cab, plus 19 ft x 30 ft C-2 quarters built partly on stilts
facts.status_note: FFLA list shows standing; the 2012 chapter report calls it abandoned and the NHLR page says awaiting restoration
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Stanislaus National Forest (Groveland Ranger District)

events.note: Register: built by the CCC from 1934-35; Built field gives 1935
Date Registered on NHLR page: June 4, 1998
Trumbull Peak Cabin Restoration (project 1665): decision signed March 24, 2009; project page lists status Completed
Motor Fire threatened the abandoned lookout; protected and saved
Trail improved in 2012; plan to make a recreation rental put on hold; tower heavily vandalized

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Service project 1665 (decision signed 2009) is marked Completed, the 2012 chapter report says the recreation rental plan was on hold, and the NHLR page says awaiting restoration. The 2009 project was for the historic cabin at the base of the lookout; the sources do not say whether the 2012 rental plan concerns the same work. The sources do not establish the current condition.

notes_for_editor: The NHLR page gives the tower as 41 ft and the CCC build as 1934-35; I used those. A web search summary mentioned a 45-ft tower from a trail guide and a Groveland office phone number; neither was fetched or verified, so neither is used. The sources do not say whether the 2009 cabin restoration and the 2012 rental plan are the same work, and no source read confirms the current condition or whether the public can visit. The record's 'abandoned' is from the 2012 report and is dated to that year. The height 12.5 m is the tower only, converted from 41 ft.
